title_html: Decide shareholders, legal representative, supervisor, and (where required) finance contact; prepare PRC ID cards and mobile numbers for real-name verification.

detail.html: Director and supervisor cannot be the same person in the standard one-shareholder layout; your filing portal will flag conflicts.

title_html: Reserve 3–5 candidate names and secure a compliant registered address—lease + property certificate, or (where permitted) a government/business-park cluster address.

detail.html: Many cities run name checks inside the same “one-stop” website; the AMR must approve the final name before issuance.

title_html: Set subscribed capital, shareholding ratios, payment timeline, and business scope (and any license-triggering lines).

detail.html: Under the 2024 Company Law, subscribed amounts must generally be fully paid within five years of incorporation unless transition rules apply—document the schedule in the articles.

title_html: File online through the provincial government service portal / enterprise “one-stop” (e.g. 开办企业一窗通)—upload IDs, address proof, generated articles, and e-sign with facial recognition.

detail.html: Optional: hire a local bookkeeping/agent firm (代办)—common for first-time founders; scope should list filing, chops, and tax onboarding.

title_html: AMR review → receive the 营业执照 (electronic license immediate in many cities; paper optional).

detail.html: Typical review windows are roughly 1–3 working days when materials are complete—longer if the name or scope needs fixes.

title_html: Carve and file official seals (公章, 财务章, 法人章, 发票章 as needed) with the public-security filing system.

detail.html: Some municipalities bundle free first seals for new market entrants—check the same one-stop portal.

money.html: Est.: if not free, a full set often ¥300–1,200; express/specialty materials extra.

title_html: Open the RMB basic bank account (基本户) with the license and seals—KYC is lighter than a WFOE but still in-person or video per bank policy.

detail.html: Shareholder capital can be wired from personal accounts per subscribed amounts—no foreign FDI account required.

title_html: Complete tax registration and enable digital invoices (数电票) with the tax bureau—often linked through the one-stop flow.

detail.html: Assign accounting rules (small-scale vs. general VAT taxpayer) with your agent or tax advisor before issuing invoices to clients.

title_html: Register for social insurance and housing fund accounts so you can hire and run payroll compliantly.

detail.html: Contribution rates follow local rules—use the same city assumptions as the dashboard for planning.

title_html: Stand up bookkeeping and periodic tax filings (monthly/quarterly VAT, annual CIT prep, payroll withholding)—in-house or via a 代理记账 firm.

detail.html: Missing filing deadlines triggers penalties—budget this before you take your first paying client.
